drhp.business: G.M. Breweries Limited manufactures and markets alcoholic beverages, blending and bottling both Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) and country liquor (CL), with concentration mainly on country liquor due to competitive conditions in the IMFL segment. The company runs a fully automated, state-of-the-art bottling plant at Virar, Palghar (Maharashtra), serving lower and middle income group consumers primarily in Mumbai, Thane and Palghar districts.
drhp.end_markets: Country liquor market in Mumbai, Thane & Palghar districts, Maharashtra|Lower and Middle Income Group customers|Sold across 1 state in India; no exports (0.00% of turnover)
drhp.expansion: No new plant, line or greenfield project is named. The company's stated expansion route is utilising its existing surplus bottling capacity (13.76 crore bulk litres per annum installed, only ~59.59% utilised last year) by extending distribution into interior districts of Maharashtra, rather than adding new capacity. Management states the existing installed capacity should suffice for at least the next five years.

litigation.note: Various industry trade bodies have filed writ petitions in the Bombay High Court challenging a Maharashtra government notification (effective April 1, 2016) banning use of PET bottles for filling alcoholic liquor; the Court admitted the petitions and granted an interim stay, which remains in force with no final judgment yet. Disclosed in the Management Discussion and Analysis Report.

drhp.one_liner: The single largest manufacturer of country liquor in the State of Maharashtra, with substantial market share concentrated in Mumbai, Thane & Palghar.

plants.capacity: Installed capacity of 13.76 crore bulk litres of country liquor per annum; can produce over 50,000 cases a day (vs initial production rate of 200 cases/day)
plants.role: Fully automated bottling plant (blends and bottles both glass and PET bottles)

risks.note: Management flags the parallel duty-evaded market as the major threat to the company, eroding both its market share and government excise revenue; the company continues to make representations to Government to curb it.

Very high levels of taxation and frequent changes in laws create difficulty for the company; management states the exorbitant tax rate is itself one of the factors that breeds duty evasion in the market.
High fluctuations in the price of Rectified Spirit, the main raw material, combined with acute shortages in its availability, have been a persistent constraint over several years.
risks.risk: Raw material (Rectified Spirit) price volatility and shortage

risks.note: PET bottles account for ~92.72% of production, so the company is exposed to sudden spurts in PET bottle prices driven by international petroleum prices and forex fluctuations, as experienced last year.

The company faces concurrent and parallel jurisdiction of multiple government agencies (State Excise Department, Legal Metrology Department, FDA) whose requirements management describes as conflicting in nature.

A Maharashtra government notification banning PET bottles for alcoholic liquor (effective April 1, 2016) is under challenge via writ petitions in the Bombay High Court, which has granted an interim stay still in force with no final judgment; management states the eventual outcome will not affect operations since all bottling lines can handle both glass and PET.
risks.risk: Pending litigation on PET bottle usage notification

risks.note: Management states that the illicit market, taxation, and input-cost/regulatory factors together are expected to have a serious impact on the business in the current financial year, but that the impact cannot be quantified or its timing forecast.
risks.risk: Unquantifiable near-term impact from combined deterrents
